1 Scientific Literature.Title: Stabilization of basic oxygen furnace slag by hot-stage carbonation treatment
1 Scientific Literature.Authors: Rafael M. Santos, Da Ling, Amin Sarvaramini, Muxing Guo, Jan Elsen, Faïçal Larachi, Georges Beaudoin, Bart Blanpain, Tom Van Gerven
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Assess hot-stage (high-temperature, gas-solid) carbonation of BOF slag during the hot-to-cold cooling path to convert free lime, reduce basicity and stabilize heavy metal leaching.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: Free lime is the main mineral carbonating directly at high temperature. Optimum carbonation temperature is just below CaCO3 stability limit: 830-850 °C at 1 atm CO2 and 750-770 °C at 0.2 atm CO2. Pressurization and steam addition add only marginally to CO2 uptake; uptake drops with particle size but basicity reduction is similar across sizes. Ba, Co and Ni leaching reduced after carbonation; V and Cr leaching increased.
1 Scientific Literature.Notes: Accepted manuscript version. Slag studied for stabilization/valorization (aggregate, construction), not as a cementitious binder; no SCM performance tests.
